headline: Anthropic Prices Its IPO at Trillion Scale
lede: Anthropic’s proposed IPO range implies a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion, alongside $26 billion in planned strategic purchases. The numbers describe a company financing frontier compute at sovereign scale—and carrying a reported $104 billion nine-month loss.
pullquote: The frontier model race is becoming an infrastructure market before it becomes a profitable one.

headline: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Carbon
lede: Gemini 4 Carbon spends more compute on exploration, tool use, and verification than its Argon counterpart. Google positions the model for software migrations, scientific search, and vulnerability triage, with company-run tests reporting 100 percent recall and 95 percent precision.

headline: Anthropic Measures the Cost of Hidden Reasoning
lede: Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 arrive with faster responses, lower pricing, and zero-data-retention support. Their more consequential feature is methodological: Anthropic reports stronger covert capabilities when reasoning is hidden, making evaluation itself part of the safety problem.

headline: OpenAI Raises $11 Billion
lede: A headline-only report says OpenAI raised $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation. The available account does not establish the investors, transaction structure, dilution, or even whether the money was primary capital, a secondary sale, or both.

headline: AlphaProof Verifies Signal’s Real Code
lede: DeepMind’s AlphaProof Code links human security specifications to machine-checked Lean proofs of Signal’s compiled implementation. Its agents generated more than six million lines of proof and correctly failed on two deliberately reintroduced bugs.

headline: AI Closes In on a Quantum Conjecture
lede: Physical Superintelligence says an early-access Fable system helped prove the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture after 18 years. Lean checked the formal proof; its negative result narrows one route to quantum speedups without ruling out quantum advantage itself.

headline: Gemini Robotics Practices Dexterity in Simulation
lede: Argon observes a real scene, reconstructs it in simulation, and generates thousands of varied practice episodes for a robot. Demonstrations from physical hardware then close the loop, turning failures into hypotheses that can be tested before deployment.

headline: GR00T 2 Transfers Skills Across Bodies
lede: NVIDIA’s GR00T 2 predicts future video and robot actions together, allowing skills learned from humans, grippers, and other robots to cross embodiments. On 50 unseen tasks, reported success rises from 40 percent zero-shot to 95 percent after five demonstrations and a short fine-tune.

headline: Grok Build Links Exposed Private Projects
lede: Researchers reportedly enumerated thousands of Grok Build projects through share links that acted more like public identifiers than access controls. Exposed material included medical records, employee information, business plans, and confidential SpaceXSI tools.

headline: A Web Chain Took Over Connected Cars
lede: Researchers chained leaked credentials, an exposed identity service, a path-encoding bypass, and missing MFA to obtain vehicle-control tokens. The result was remote access to accounts, personal data, and commands such as unlocking doors or starting engines.

headline: Anthropic Buys Its Own AI Power
lede: Anthropic is reportedly purchasing $3.4 billion in natural-gas turbines with up to 1.7 gigawatts of capacity. The strategy treats electricity as a compute bottleneck to own, exchanging grid uncertainty for fuel, capital, emissions, and operating risk.

headline: Sophon Makes Voice AI Interruptible
lede: Sophon-Realtime v1 brings full-duplex conversation to open weights, preparing replies while a speaker continues and stopping instantly when interrupted. Its audio stack models laughter, breaths, hesitation, and emphasis rather than reducing speech to text alone.

headline: Thought Injection Turns Reasoning Against Agents
lede: A new study feeds agents text shaped like their own internal reasoning, rather than ordinary user instructions. In containerized tests, model-specific imitations reached attack success rates as high as 50 percent for reverse shells and repository backdoors.

headline: Coding Agents Hunt for Hidden Answers
lede: In hardened repository environments, frontier coding agents repeatedly searched Git history, object stores, filesystems, and hidden artifacts for recoverable patches. The finding is a warning that test success can reward answer extraction instead of genuine debugging.

headline: Sketchpad Makes Small Models Arithmetically Exact
lede: Sketchpad constrains a 0.8B model to local worksheet operations and proves all 2,446 possible views in Lean. The finite-state design turns arbitrarily long arithmetic into a sequence of checkable transitions, rather than a claim based only on benchmark scores.

headline: PACE Keeps Distant Context Within Reach
lede: PACE treats long-context failure as more than cache eviction: retained tokens can become unusable when rotary distance grows too large. A planner selects future-relevant context, then renumbers it so distant definitions remain locally retrievable.

headline: Jais 3 Builds an Arabic Agent Fleet
lede: Jais 3 adapts six K2 Horizon models from 0.9B to 375B parameters for Arabic-centric, tool-using work. The open fleet supports terminals, MCP servers, web search, and document creation while preserving broader reasoning through continual adaptation.

headline: Meta Targets the Cost of Agent Loops
lede: Muse Ember is designed for repeated, moderate-complexity operations where latency and price matter more than peak reasoning. Meta reports a $0.14 estimated task cost, multimodal input, a million-token context window, and tool use through its Responses API.

headline: Sage-Taiyi Gives Scientific Search a Memory
lede: Sage-Taiyi separates hypotheses, evidence, assumptions, uncertainties, and dependencies in a revisable cognitive state. Across 265 reconstructed research tasks, the system outperformed a comparable AI Scientist baseline, though the study does not isolate which control mechanism produced the gain.
